subject: Can RApache use AddType like mod_perl and mod_php?

messages.author: b75df6bb42949437
messages.subject: Can RApache use AddType like mod_perl and mod_php?
parts:
Hello,

I know I can use <Files>SetHandler r-info</Files> to the same effect, but it's be nice if RApache also supported syntax like Mod_Perl and mod_php i.e:
AddType application/x-httpd-perl .pl .cgi
AddType application/x-httpd-php .phtml 

Justin

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: Can RApache use AddType like mod_perl and mod_php?
parts:
Hmm...

AddType application/x-httpd-r-brew .brew

That might be possible, but it presumes that all you have is brew scripts

Or maybe:

REvalOnStartup "my.source <- function(file,env) with(data=env,source(file))"
AddType application/x-httpd-r-my.source .rhtml

Would that work?

messages.author: b75df6bb42949437
messages.subject: Re: Can RApache use AddType like mod_perl and mod_php?
parts:
I like the idea of both. Syntatic sugar for the common cases, and something that lets you handle the weird cases. Weird cases can also mean I set default plotting to a temp file  in a try catch, and unlink the file in the catch.

So maybe this:

  • AddType application/x-httpd-r-brew .brew # Executes as a brew script
  • AddType application/x-httpd-r # Executes directly in R
  • AddType application/x-httpd-r-source # Displays a syntax highlighted version of the R script see http://us1.php.net/manual/en/install.unix.apache2.php
  • AddType application/x-httpd-r-exec._FOO_ .rhtml # executes a function called exec._FOO_ 
I've never hacked on apache before, but if you implemented the last one I could probably do the other ones.

Justin

messages.subject: Re: Can RApache use AddType like mod_perl and mod_php?
parts:
Ok forget everything I said before I was completely wrong. I''ve actually read  the source for mod_R, mod_php, mod_wsgi.

So I can avoid <Directory> <Location> and <Files> and have a global config similar to mod_php if I do this:

LoadModule R_module modules/mod_R.so
AddHandler r-script .r
RHandler sys.source

I'm trying to figure out a clean way  handle both brew and r using a config like that based on file extension. I'm thinking the cleanest way would be an r package (written in C for performance) with a function that looks at the file name and executes sys.source or brew::brew based on the extension, and I set that as RHandler. Thoughts?
